name: dns_record_validator
description:
Guard for LLM-proposed DNS record changes as a single triage node. The model
proposes one typed DNS change (request_id + action add/modify/delete + a
non-empty records list of {type, name, value, ttl?}); this workflow owns schema
validation, the record-count cap, blocked record types, blocked domains, the
ttl minimum and the approval escalation. Port of
code/qwen_vm/app_scenarios/dns_record_validator.
Folding boundaries (documented, not computed in the DSL):
- JSON parsing details (required fields, request_id grammar, valid record type
enum, non-empty name/value, non-negative ttl, dangerous-token rejection) fold
into the `proposal` choice.
- The local policy table (max_records, blocked_types, blocked_domains, min_ttl,
require_approval) is a fixed fixture; each deterministic check against it
folds into one verdict choice.
Emitted labels: reject_proposal, reject_too_many_records, reject_blocked_type,
reject_blocked_domain, reject_ttl_below_min, escalate_approval, approve.

proposal.instructions: Does the model response parse as exactly one {request_id, action:add|modify|delete, records:[{type, name, value, ttl?}]} object (request_id grammar, valid type enum, non-empty name/value, non-negative integer ttl, no dangerous tokens)?

criteria.malformed: parse error, missing field, bad request_id, invalid type, bad ttl or dangerous token

record_count.instructions: Is the number of records within the policy max_records cap?

record_type.instructions: Is every record type outside the policy blocked_types set?

criteria.ok: no record uses a blocked type
criteria.blocked: at least one record uses a blocked type

domain.instructions: Is every record name outside the policy blocked_domains set?

criteria.ok: no record hits a blocked domain
criteria.blocked: at least one record hits a blocked domain

ttl.instructions: Is every record ttl at or above the policy min_ttl?

approval.instructions: Does the local policy require human approval for this DNS change?
